description: The message box at the bottom of the Baude main window's chat column: an attachments strip (only while something is attached), then a rounded card holding the text, with the attach and send buttons in its bottom-right corner. Messages queued or held while the agent works are drawn in the chat column just above it (see parts).

parts.name: text box
parts.shows: A card with the text in the chat's font (scales with chat zoom), word-wrapped. Empty or one line, it is wrapped close round its buttons: as tall as a button (composer.button, 28 px) with the buttons' inset (composer.inset, 4 px) above and below, the line centred on the buttons, the same height as a side question's box under its question (SideQuestions). Where the line is taller than the buttons (a large chat zoom, Text size or Global Scale) or the buttons taller than 28 px (a large Icons size), the one-line box is the taller of the two plus the inset above and below, and both are centred in it. As the text grows the buttons stay at the bottom, centred on its last line. The box follows a change of zoom or size at once, smaller as well as larger. It grows with the text and scrolls past about nine lines (220 px), its scrollbar shown only then. Until then it fits its text exactly in every frame, a line just wrapped included: never scrolled, its top line never cut and no gap left at its bottom. The right margin keeps text from running under the buttons. No placeholder text. Spell check is not on in Baude's box (it is a Record page feature). The box takes the focus when a window opens; a click anywhere in the card puts the caret in the text. A host's chat's text is its host's draft (schema/types/DraftSave.request.json): the box opens with it and follows other heads' edits to it; what was sent from any box never comes back into it.

actions.does: A new line; on a list item the next item (bullet or number continued); on an empty list item it leaves the list; in a code block a plain new line, and an unclosed block gets its closing fence at once
A plain line break (no list continuation)
Sends. While the agent is working the text is queued instead (see queued messages)
While a turn is running: stops it (interrupt); background commands and subagents go on (BackgroundTask). With a revert pending: cancels the revert. With a completer list open: closes the list first
On list items or a selection of them: in or out one level (a bullet 2 spaces); in a code block: four spaces in or out; elsewhere moves the focus
Moves the list item the caret is in past its neighbour
Leaves a just-formatted run (after wrap-selection) to outside its marks
Pastes text as text; copied files or a copied image are attached instead (see attachments). Ctrl+V pastes on a Mac too

Wraps the selection: * makes it bold (**…**), ` makes it code (`…`), / makes it italic (*…*); each line of a multi-line selection wrapped on its own, list markers, headings and quotes left out; stays selected so another mark can go round it (* then /: bold italic); typing the same mark again unwraps it

parts.name: markdown shown as typed

decisions.said: In every formatted input box, > shows as a quote as it does once sent
decisions.rule: Every app's formatted boxes (the chat's, Meta's, Send Feedback's) show a line starting with > as a quote while it's written, as a sent quote looks: a rule at its left, its text set in past it and faded, not italic, the > hidden off the caret's line

parts.shows: The text is styled live like chat messages while still plain text: # headings at the chat's heading sizes, **bold**, *italic*, `inline code` (monospace, shaded), ``` fenced code blocks (one rounded shaded background behind all lines, fence lines dim, monospace), bullet lists with real bullets (- * + typed become • at the top level, ◦ one level in; sent back as -) with hanging indent, numbered lists, > quotes. Markdown symbols (#, **, `) are hidden except on the line the caret is on, where they show dim. @names the catalogue knows are coloured (green, bold, tinted background), and the @ search being typed too.

decisions.said: Being unable to paste images and such into the input is a massive oversight (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: In every app, pasting copied images or files into a message box (any paste: Ctrl+V, ⌘V, Shift+Insert, the menu's Paste) attaches them; text pastes as text

decisions.said: Tab in the agent's box should indent (bullet points), as it does in Record; right now it's unclear what it does (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: In every app's message boxes Tab moves the list item (or selected items) in a level and Shift+Tab out, as on a Record page; in a code block it indents four spaces; elsewhere it moves the focus

decisions.said: Across both mobile and desktop, the default height of the prompt bar bar can be shrunk. A good reference is the one that currently exists for side questions post-initial-ask. I.e. the default bar is just closely wrapperd around the "+" and "Enter" icon
decisions.rule: Every app's empty or one-line message box is wrapped close round its buttons: a button's height with the buttons' inset above and below (composer tokens), the same height as a side question's box under its question; it grows with the text

decisions.said: Thread drafts need to be saved across the mesh
decisions.rule: Every app keeps a host chat's unsent text on the chat's host, not on the device: any head on any machine that opens the chat shows the same draft, and an edit in one shows in the others. A head saves about 400 ms after typing stops, at once when the box is emptied (a message sent or queued), and as the chat is left. Sending clears the draft everywhere. When two heads type at once the last write the host takes wins; a head's own save coming back never replaces what it has typed since. Only the text is shared: attachments are files on the device and stay with it.

decisions.said: Draft sync doesn't refresh while the pointer rests on the box; hovering mustn't stop updates from the draft's owner (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Nothing about the pointer, the focus or the window being in front keeps another head's edit out of a box: it goes in unless this head has typing its host hasn't taken yet, or a save on its way, and the caret and selection move with the text. Text this head typed that the host never took is never replaced by another head's edit: a draft over 200000 characters (which the host refuses) stays this head's own and is not saved again, and an edit held meanwhile stays held; a save lost to a dropped connection leaves the box dirty and is made again after 1 s, then 2 s, then 4 s (and as the chat is attached again), an edit held from before the typing staying held.

decisions.said: There seems to be an issue with drafts coming back to me post send. In think this would be fixed if we used some id ber enter-invocation to prevent splashback
decisions.rule: Text a head has sent never comes back into any box. Every Enter (or Send) that empties a box is a send with an id of its own: its save empties the host's draft and starts the draft's next epoch, and the same send's save made again empties it once. Every save says the epoch its text was written in; the host refuses one from an earlier epoch, and every head drops a draft from an epoch earlier than one it has seen. A head typing on text that another head then sends keeps only what it typed itself, the sent text taken out of its box, and saves that; text a head typed that the host never took is still never replaced by another head's edit. The phone's own sends empty the host's draft as the desktop's do.

decisions.said: The text in the chat box keeps getting its top line cut off even though the box has room to grow, leaving empty padding at the bottom; as lines wrap it goes perfect, overflow, half cut off at the top and half space at the bottom, perfect, and repeats (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's message box fits its text exactly at every step as it grows or shrinks, the frame a line wraps included, and scrolls only once the text is past its tallest; the caret's own scroll into sight never leaves a box that holds all its text scrolled.

source.relayed: the owner's report, passed on by the coordinator on 2026-11-28 (no Claude Code message uuid found)

parts.name: attach button
parts.shows: A flat button with a + (list-add) icon, left of the send button, bottom right of the card: 28 px square (composer.button), 4 px apart.

actions.does: Tooltip "Attach images, PDFs or files (or paste / drop them)"
Opens a file chooser titled "Attach files", multi-select, filters "All files" and "Images & PDFs"; each chosen file is attached

parts.name: send / stop button
parts.shows: A round icon button, last in the corner, 28 px square (composer.button), 4 px in from the card's right and bottom edges (composer.inset), centred on the text's last line at any text or icon size. Idle: grey, a return-arrow icon. While the agent works: red (destructive), a stop square icon.
text:
Send ({key})
New line: Enter
@: a chat, a file, a pull request…

actions.does: Tooltip "Send (Ctrl+Enter)" then "New line: Enter" then "@: a chat, a file, a pull request…" (⌘Enter on a Mac)
Tooltip "Stop (Esc)"

Sends the text and attachments (markdown, bullets turned back to -). Nothing is sent when both are empty. A first message after viewing a past session resumes that session. The box and strip empty and the chat scrolls to the end
Stops the turn (also with a revert pending); background commands and subagents go on (BackgroundTask). Enter/Ctrl+Enter with text meanwhile queues instead of stopping

decisions.said: On desktop, sometimes the new narrow "Enter" button is not center aligned vertically please investigate and fix this
decisions.rule: Every app keeps the message box's buttons centred on the text's line at every text and icon size, and after the text grows or shrinks (zoom, Text size)

parts.name: slash commands in the box
parts.shows: Typing / at the start of the prompt (or at a word's start after a space or new line) opens a command list over the box; see SlashCompleter. These commands are handled by Baude itself and never sent: /new and /clear (a fresh session, on the open chat's host: another host's chat gets a blank chat on that host, in its folder), /cd <path> (move the conversation to another folder), /btw <question> (side question, answered without adding to the chat; works mid-turn), /login [options] and /logout (Anthropic account sign-in; /login on another host's chat says it signs in there: run claude auth login on it).

parts.name: @ references in the box
parts.shows: Typing @ at a word's start opens a list of chats and the names of the chat's folder; see MentionCompleter.

parts.name: attachments strip
parts.shows: A row above the card, hidden until something is attached, scrolling sideways. Each attachment is a chip: an image as a 48 px square centre-cropped thumbnail; a PDF or other file as its type icon (or the system thumbnail where one exists) and its file name (… in the middle past 22 characters); a small round × button at the end of each. Images are shrunk/recompressed for the model; a pasted image is named "pasted image.png".

actions.does: Tooltip: the file's full path, or its name for a pasted image
Opens the image viewer over the window
Removes that attachment (tooltip "Remove")

Copied files are attached. A copied image is attached; an image copied together with text is attached when the text is only its file name or web address, otherwise the text is pasted. Copied web addresses that aren't local files fall back to the image beside them, else the text

actions.by: drag and drop onto the window
actions.does: Files or an image dropped anywhere on the window are attached and the focus goes to the box; ignored while the chat is read-only
A quiet note in the chat: "can't attach <path>: not a file", "can't attach image: <error>", or "paste failed: <error>"

parts.name: queued messages
parts.shows: A message sent while the agent is mid-turn is drawn as a grey user bubble under the conversation (above the box) instead of being sent. It carries its attachments.

actions.does: Three small round buttons fade in left of the bubble, level with its last line
Drops the message (tooltip "Delete this queued message")

Sends this message and every one queued before it together as one message, to the turn going on, which goes on, its foreground commands and subagents moved to the background in a Claude Code chat so it takes the message in now (tooltip "Send now: send this and the queued messages before it, without stopping the chat")
Takes it out of the queue and puts its text before what is in the box, with its attachments, and focuses the box (tooltip "Edit: put this message back in the box")
All queued messages are sent together as one message, in order. A turn stopped with Esc or the stop button leaves them queued
The queue is kept with its chat, drawn again under it when it's opened, and sent to it when its turn ends meanwhile (see QueuedTurn)

parts.name: held messages
parts.shows: A message the chat's host held rather than sent (a subagent's answer that arrived after the host restarted) is drawn grey in the same place as queued ones, above them, from whom it came shown at its top (its sender), in the order held.

actions.does: Two small round buttons fade in: ✕ and ↑
Drops it on its host (tooltip "Delete this held message"); a refusal toasts "Not deleted: <why>"

Sends it to the chat (tooltip "Send it to the chat: it was held, not sent, as this chat's host restarted while it waited for it"). Toasts when it can't: "It can be sent once this turn's over", "It can't be sent while this chat's context is exhausted: pick a model with a bigger window, or clear it", "It can't be sent while the connection to this chat's host is down", "It can't be sent while this chat's host isn't there", or "It can't be sent while nothing can be sent in this chat"; "Not sent: <why>" if the host refuses

states.name: working
states.shows: Red stop button; text sent meanwhile is queued, grey, under the conversation

states.name: context exhausted
states.shows: A plain grey line "Context Exhausted" just above the card; the send button is off (Enter and Ctrl+Enter too, except /clear /new /cd /login /logout); the box stays editable. Cleared by picking a model with a bigger window or clearing the chat; hidden again while a turn runs

states.name: host gone or connection dropped
states.shows: The send button is off (nothing to send to) while a banner above the chat says why (see Banners); the box stays editable. On an app whose link the OS closes (the phone), the send button stays on while the host isn't reached: what's sent is queued under the chat with a cloud beside it, kept on disk, and sent once the host is back (see QueuedTurn).

decisions.said: Nearly all of the phone's disconnects come from the screen turning off or the app being put away: design for Android closing connections, cache more, and instead of a red box show a cloud, with leeway and messages queued while the connection is down (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app whose link the OS or browser closes lets you send while a host isn't reached: the message is queued, marked as waiting for its host, and sent by itself once the host is back and the chat has caught up.

states.name: read-only by choice
states.shows: ☰ → Read-only session: the whole box is gone (not greyed). If the box had the focus, the focus moves to the chat. Remembered per chat

states.name: active elsewhere
states.shows: A Claude Desktop chat being written right now by Claude Desktop: the box is gone and the banner "This session is currently active elsewhere" is shown, until it has been quiet for a while. Only Claude Desktop's chats are guarded this way; any other chat (a host's, another window's, a terminal's) can be written to

states.name: draft kept
states.shows: Each chat keeps its own draft (text, caret, attachments) while another chat is open, and over a restart; a new chat keeps one shared draft

decisions.said: Drafts are shared across chats; a draft should belong to the Bot or chat it was written in (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app keeps each chat's (and Bot's) draft on its own: text, caret and attachments come back when the chat is opened again, and another chat's box shows its own draft or nothing

states.name: revert pending
states.shows: After Revert on a sent message the text is in the box for editing; Enter-send commits the revert then sends; Esc cancels it
